label: Blackfoot Draw: repeated repaired_in_place on conductor_or_connector with declining benefit
headline: Blackfoot Draw's 'declining repair effectiveness' is a tagging artifact — three unrelated failure modes merged under one component label with zero recorded benefit data — and the only real item inside it is a routine clip upgrade on three blocks that belongs in the next mow-cycle cable pass.
action: Split the 'conductor_or_connector' tag into termination/connector vs cable-support before re-running the efficacy detector, and confirm whether the recurrence flag on WO-2026-00564 is linked to a prior WO ID or only inferred from free text; separately, add the heavier north-block clip to the next scheduled mow-cycle cable pass on B02/B03/B04 as routine work, not as an escalation.
reasoning: The 'declining benefit' claim has no quantitative basis: benefit_pct is null on all five members, so mean_benefit_early/late and benefit_drop are null, and late_ineffective_share of 0.33 is a single recurrence flag (WO-2026-00564) out of three late WOs — text-derived from the tech's own phrase 'second rework on this block inside a year'. The five members are also mechanistically unrelated: burned MC4 terminations with connector parts consumed (WO-2025-00971, WO-2026-00455), cable sag/clip-fixing rework with no parts (WO-2025-01233, WO-2026-00564), and a chafed home-run ground fault (WO-2026-00462); they share no asset IDs across modes and carry inconsistent resolution codes (PART-REPL, RESET, OTHER) for the same nominal action. The controls confirm the chafe/ground-fault mode is fleet baseline, not a Blackfoot Draw efficacy problem — near-identical narratives appear at Bitter Draw (WO-2025-00367), Caprock Mesa (WO-2026-00536, WO-2024-00002) and Sandhill Bend (WO-2025-00524), all closing resolved at comparable labor hours. H1 captures a real but narrow observation (clip-fixing failure on B02/B04, with the heavier clip already proven on the north blocks) and H3 a plausible connector story, but neither is what this cluster measures, and neither is separable at n=2 per mode; H4's baseline framing is consistent with the controls. The correct read is that the coarse 'conductor_or_connector' tag merged two-to-three populations and manufactured a trend out of one flag.
contradicting: WO-2026-00564 is a genuine second cable-management rework on B04 within a year, with a specific, credible root cause named by the tech (failure at the clip fixing, not cable pull-through) and a specific fix already validated on the north blocks; WO-2025-01233 shows the same clip-fixing mode on B02 and WO-2026-00141 flags pending cable sag on B03. That is a real, if small, site-level workmanship/hardware issue that this decline does not dispute — it is simply not an efficacy-decay signal and does not carry material MWh exposure at P2/P3 with ~21 total labor hours over eight months.

population_detail.description: Blackfoot Draw blocks with light-type cable clips on home runs: B02 and B04 (already reworked) and B03 (cable sag flagged, work pending). Not a fleet-wide population; the burned-connector and chafe modes show no repeat asset IDs.
population_detail.basis: Distinct asset_ids in WO-2025-01233 (B02), WO-2026-00564 (B04) and WO-2026-00141 (B03); no block-count or string-count denominator for Blackfoot Draw was provided, so this is an observed-block count, not a modelled exposure.

hypotheses.statement: Blackfoot Draw blocks B02/B04 were built with an undersized cable-clip fixing that fails at the fixing point, and repaired_in_place reworks that re-use the same light clip do not arrest the failure, producing genuine repeat work on the same rows.
predictions: Repeat repaired_in_place work orders on the same block IDs (B02, B04) at intervals under ~12 months, with narratives naming clip/fixing failure rather than cable pull-through.
Work orders on the 'north blocks' (where the heavier clip was already fitted) show no cable-management repeats over the same span.
Parts_used on these cable-management WOs is blank or generic (no clip part number issued), consistent with re-securing with existing hardware.
Subsequent DC ground-fault or arc WOs at this site isolate to home runs on the same blocks (e.g. CB-B03-17-type locations), i.e. chafe faults trail the sag repairs.
Labor hours per cable-management WO stay flat or rise (~4-5 h) rather than falling with experience.
discriminating_evidence: A WO where the heavier clip part is actually issued and consumed, followed by no recurrence on that row for >12 months, confirms the clip-type mechanism.
If repeat WOs land on rows that were never previously reworked (fresh rows each time), the 'repair doesn't hold' story fails and this is a fleet-wide install issue instead.
Presence/absence of the same clip-fixing language at other sites built by the same contractor separates site-specific from design-wide.

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is a grouping artifact: five work orders spanning two mechanistically unrelated failure modes (burned MC4 terminations vs. sagging cable clips) were merged by the coarse 'conductor_or_connector' component tag, and the 'declining benefit' signal is entirely one recurrence flag out of three late WOs with no benefit_pct recorded anywhere.
predictions: mean_benefit_early_pct, mean_benefit_late_pct and benefit_drop_pct remain null across all five members — no quantitative efficacy series exists to decay.
late_ineffective_share of 0.33 decomposes to exactly 1 recurrence flag in 3 late WOs; removing or re-dating that single WO collapses the trend.
Splitting the cluster by symptom yields two sub-groups (component_thermal_damage with MC4 parts and PART-REPL codes; physical_damage/corrosion_or_wear with no parts) that share no asset IDs.
Resolution codes are inconsistent (PART-REPL, RESET, OTHER) for nominally the same action, indicating loose coding rather than a coherent repair population.
Similar 5-member 'efficacy_decay' candidates appear at other sites for the same component tag with equally null benefit fields.
discriminating_evidence: Re-run the decay detector with component split into 'connector/termination' vs 'cable management/support' — if neither sub-cluster shows a trend, the signal is an aggregation artifact.

Check whether the recurrence flag is set by extraction from free text ('second rework on this block') rather than by linkage to a prior WO ID; text-only recurrence flags inflate late-ineffective share.
Bootstrap the ineffective share on n=5: if the 95% interval spans 0 to >0.6, the decay is not distinguishable from noise.

hypotheses.statement: Burned MC4 home-run terminations at Blackfoot Draw are a separate, real connector-population defect (cross-mated or poorly crimped connectors) that cut-and-reterminate fixes permanently at the repaired point but which will keep surfacing at new locations across the same connector lot.
predictions: Thermal-damage WOs each name a different string/home run; no asset ID repeats for the burn mode specifically.
Every thermal WO consumes an MC4 connector part and closes as PART-REPL with outcome 'resolved' and recurrence false.
Arrival rate of burn WOs is roughly steady or increasing over the span rather than clustering in one month.
Reported lost MWh per burn WO is larger than per cable-management WO, since a burn opens a string while a sag does not.
discriminating_evidence: If a re-terminated home run burns again at the same repaired joint, the repair itself is the problem (workmanship), not the connector lot.
If burn WOs concentrate in blocks fed by one combiner or one install crew, it is a lot/crew defect; if uniformly spread, it is a general population wear mode.
Absence of any burn WOs at the same site before 2025-10 would argue for an ageing/lot effect rather than an install defect.

hypotheses.statement: This is ordinary corrective volume for the installed base: five conductor/connector CM work orders over ~8 months (21 labor hours, 14 MWh) at one site is an unremarkable rate, and the apparent pairing of cable-management jobs is driven by mow-cycle scheduling that surfaces sagging runs seasonally.
predictions: Normalising by block or string count at Blackfoot Draw gives a conductor/connector CM rate within the range of peer sites in the corpus.
Cable-management WOs cluster immediately before or during mow windows (Dec and May/June entries here), with none in the off-mow period.
Priorities stay P2/P3 with no escalation to P1 and no repair-hour growth across the span.
No trend in lost_mwh_reported per WO from early to late members.
discriminating_evidence: Compare Blackfoot Draw's per-block conductor/connector WO count against all other sites over the same window; an unexceptional percentile supports this hypothesis over H1/H3.
If sag-related WOs occur outside mow windows at the same rate, the seasonal-inspection explanation fails.
If the same site shows the same five-WO pattern in the prior year with no growth, the 'decay' is baseline; if this window is the first occurrence, a defect explanation gains weight.

exposure_note: Priced at the cost model's inverter replacement rate. This population is not inverters, so treat the count as the reliable figure and this dollar value as indicative only.
